endpoints.help: The saved endpoints in list order. Each holds an address for GET requests, headers, column mappings, a write mode and a schedule. Mappings and write mode are stored but not applied yet: a fetch writes nothing into the worksheet.

id.help: The identifier of the endpoint; it stays the same when renaming.

name.help: The name of the endpoint in the list on the left; when empty the list shows a placeholder.

url.help: The address to which Send and the automatic polling send a GET request. Any text, not validated; if it is empty, Send is rejected with "Please enter a URL.". The app only allows requests to its own origin; a foreign address yields status 0.

headers.help: Additional request headers, such as an access key, each with name and value. Headers without a name are not sent. Values of secret headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, X-API-Key and any name containing token, secret, key or auth) appear as •••• when the agent reads and in the project export; an imported project needs them again.

key.help: The name of the header, such as Authorization or Accept; surrounding spaces are removed when sending.

value.help: The value of the header, sent unchanged. The placeholder •••• is not a valid value.

mappings.help: Mappings from a path in the JSON response to a column in the worksheet. They are stored but not applied yet. Within an endpoint, a column belongs to at most one mapping.

jsonPath.help: The path in the JSON response in dot notation, such as data.values.

columnRef.help: The target column in the worksheet; empty while none is chosen.

writeMode.help: How mapped data is to be written into the columns: clear columns before writing, append data at the end or insert data at the top. Stored, but without effect yet, because mappings are not applied yet.

schedule.help: The schedule of the automatic polling. It only runs while the module is open and a URL is set; only one fetch runs at a time, a fetch that falls due during a running one is skipped.

enabled.help: Automatic polling on or off. Without a URL it has no effect until a URL is set.

intervalValue.help: The gap between two fetches as a whole number from 1 to 999, together with the unit next to it. Any other value is an error. Changing it while the schedule runs restarts the schedule; disabled while automatic polling is off.

intervalUnit.help: The unit of the gap: minutes or hours.

activeId.help: The endpoint the view on the right shows. Only the user interface selects it.

scheduleWithoutUrl.help: The identifiers of the endpoints whose automatic polling is switched on but which have no URL; no fetch runs for them.

secretHeadersEmpty.help: The secret headers without a value, each with endpoint, position and name — for example after importing a project whose export had masked the values. They must be entered again.

addEndpoint.help: Adds a new, empty endpoint and shows it. The agent receives the identifier of the new endpoint.

params.command: An empty object; the command takes no arguments.

selectEndpoint.help: Shows an endpoint in the view on the right; only through the user interface (click on the list entry or into its name field).

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.

renameEndpoint.help: Renames an endpoint; it does not have to be the one shown.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.name: The new name; the empty text clears it.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId and name.

removeEndpoint.help: Removes an endpoint including its schedule. If it was the one shown, the first remaining one is shown. The user interface asks first.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId.

addHeader.help: Add header appends an empty header to the endpoint. The agent receives its position in the list of headers.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId.

setHeader.help: Sets name and value of a header of the endpoint.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.index: The position of the header, counted from 0. A position without a header is an error.
params.key: The name of the header; the empty text clears it.
params.value: The value of the header; the empty text clears it.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId, index, key and value.

removeHeader.help: Deletes a header of the endpoint.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.index: The position of the header, counted from 0. A position without a header is an error.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId and index.

addMapping.help: Add mapping appends an empty mapping between a path of the response and a column to the endpoint. Mappings are stored but not applied yet. The agent receives its position in the list of mappings.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId.

setMapping.help: Sets path and target column of a mapping of the endpoint. A column already used by another mapping of this endpoint is an error.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.index: The position of the mapping, counted from 0. A position without a mapping is an error.
params.jsonPath: The path in the JSON response; the empty text clears it.
params.ref: The target column as a column reference with instanceId, sheetId and columnId, or empty to release the mapping.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId, index, jsonPath and ref.

removeMapping.help: Deletes a mapping of the endpoint.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.
params.index: The position of the mapping, counted from 0. A position without a mapping is an error.
params.command: The command as an object with endpointId and index.
The command as an object with endpointId.

sendRequest.help: Send performs a GET request to the URL of the endpoint and waits for the response; the agent receives it as the result (status, status text, success, content), the user interface shows it under Response. The request goes over the network; the app only allows its own origin. A network error or unreadable JSON yields status 0 with the error message as content. Without a URL the fetch is rejected. Only one fetch runs at a time, across endpoints too.

params.endpointId: The identifier of an endpoint as read() lists it in the endpoint list. An unknown identifier is an error.

cancel.help: Cancels the running fetch; the response of the endpoint stays empty. Without a fetch nothing happens.

Response.status: The HTTP status of the response, such as 200 or 404; 0 when no response could be read (network error, blocked origin, unreadable JSON).
Response.statusText: The status text for the status, such as OK; Error when no response could be read.
Response.ok: Whether the status is between 200 and 299.
Response.body: The content of the response: JSON indented by two spaces, otherwise the text; on an error the error message.

SecretGap.index: The position of the header, counted from 0.
